system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Focal seizures arising from temporal lobe networks can cause an aura, impaired awareness, automatisms, and postictal confusion.
vignette: A 27-year-old man has episodes beginning with a rising epigastric sensation followed by lip smacking, staring, and 2 minutes of impaired awareness with brief confusion afterward.
correct: Focal impaired-awareness seizure of temporal lobe origin
distractor_notes: Absence seizures are brief, occur mainly in children, and lack postictal confusion.
Generalized tonic-clonic seizures include bilateral convulsions.
Syncope causes transient loss of consciousness from cerebral hypoperfusion and usually lacks stereotyped automatisms and aura.
Panic attacks do not cause impaired awareness with postictal confusion.
key_expl: Aura, automatisms, impaired awareness, and postictal confusion are classic for temporal-lobe focal impaired-awareness seizures.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Prolonged seizure activity causes excessive neuronal excitation, metabolic demand, excitotoxic injury, and systemic complications.
vignette: A patient has continuous generalized convulsions for more than 5 minutes without regaining consciousness.
lead: Which pathophysiologic process makes prolonged seizure activity dangerous?
correct: Sustained excitatory neuronal activity with high metabolic demand and excitotoxic injury
distractors: Progressive suppression of glutamate release only
distractor_notes: Status epilepticus reflects persistent neuronal firing, not electrical silence.
Excitatory neurotransmission persists rather than being selectively suppressed.
Autonomic activation often increases during seizures.
The injury is systemic and cerebral, not limited to the retina.
key_expl: Persistent synchronous neuronal firing greatly increases cerebral metabolic demand and can cause excitotoxic neuronal injury.
objective: Explain the danger of prolonged convulsive status epilepticus.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Misfolded prion protein induces conformational conversion of normal prion protein, causing rapidly progressive spongiform neurodegeneration.
vignette: A 66-year-old man develops rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus, and ataxia over 4 months.
distractor_notes: Alzheimer disease progresses over years, not a few months.
Lewy body dementia is more gradual and features hallucinations and parkinsonism.
Frontotemporal dementia often begins with behavior or language changes and is less explosively progressive.
Normal pressure hydrocephalus causes gait, cognition, and urinary symptoms.
key_expl: Very rapidly progressive dementia with myoclonus and ataxia strongly suggests prion disease.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Radial nerve injury in the spiral groove weakens wrist and finger extensors and can impair dorsal hand sensation.
vignette: A man sleeps with his arm draped over a chair and awakens unable to extend his wrist.
distractor_notes: Median nerve injury impairs thenar function and lateral-hand sensation.
Ulnar nerve injury affects intrinsic hand muscles and medial digits.
Axillary nerve injury affects deltoid function.
Musculocutaneous nerve injury affects elbow flexion.
key_expl: Radial neuropathy causes wrist drop from loss of wrist extensor function.
objective: Localize wrist drop to radial nerve injury.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Compression near the fibular neck injures the common fibular nerve, causing foot drop from weak dorsiflexion and sensory loss over the dorsum of the foot.
vignette: After prolonged leg crossing, a patient develops foot drop and numbness over the dorsum of the foot.
lead: Which nerve is most likely injured?
distractors: Sciatic nerve at the pelvis only
distractor_notes: Tibial nerve injury weakens plantarflexion and affects sole sensation.
Femoral nerve injury impairs knee extension.
Obturator nerve injury impairs thigh adduction.
A proximal sciatic lesion would usually affect both tibial and fibular divisions more broadly.
key_expl: The common fibular nerve is vulnerable at the fibular neck and injury produces foot drop.
objective: Localize foot drop after fibular-neck compression.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Dorsal columns carry ipsilateral vibration, fine touch, and conscious proprioception in the spinal cord before crossing in the medulla.
vignette: A patient has a right posterior column lesion at T10.
lead: Which sensory deficit is expected below the lesion?
correct: Right-sided loss of vibration and proprioception
distractors: Left-sided loss of pain and temperature only
Right-sided loss of motor strength only
distractor_notes: Spinothalamic tracts carry pain/temperature and cross near entry.
Motor strength is corticospinal, not dorsal column function.
Visual pathways are unrelated.
Facial sensation is carried by trigeminal pathways.
key_expl: Spinal dorsal-column fibers ascend ipsilaterally until they cross in the medulla.
objective: Predict sensory deficits from a dorsal-column spinal lesion.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Pain-temperature fibers enter the spinal cord, ascend or descend a few segments, cross in the anterior white commissure, and then ascend contralaterally.
vignette: A left anterolateral spinal cord lesion is present at T8.
lead: Which deficit is expected below the lesion?
correct: Right-sided loss of pain and temperature beginning a few segments below
distractors: Left-sided loss of vibration and proprioception
distractor_notes: Vibration and proprioception travel in dorsal columns.
Facial motor function is mediated by CN VII.
Monocular blindness is optic nerve disease.
Hearing loss is unrelated to thoracic spinothalamic tracts.
key_expl: Spinothalamic fibers cross near the spinal level of entry, so a left tract lesion causes contralateral pain-temperature loss.
objective: Predict deficits from an anterolateral spinal cord lesion.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: CN III innervates most extraocular muscles, levator palpebrae, and parasympathetic pupillary constrictor pathways; lesions cause ptosis, down-and-out eye, and possible mydriasis.
vignette: A patient has ptosis, a dilated pupil, and the affected eye rests down and out.
distractor_notes: CN IV palsy impairs superior oblique function.
CN V mediates facial sensation and mastication.
CN VI palsy impairs lateral rectus abduction.
CN VII palsy affects facial expression.
key_expl: CN III palsy causes ptosis, impaired adduction/elevation/depression, and parasympathetic pupillary dysfunction.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: CN VI innervates the lateral rectus; injury prevents abduction and causes horizontal diplopia.
vignette: A patient cannot abduct the right eye and has horizontal diplopia that worsens when looking right.
distractor_notes: Medial rectus is innervated by CN III.
Superior oblique is innervated by CN IV.
Inferior oblique is innervated by CN III.
The deficit is in the right eye, not left.
key_expl: The abducens nerve innervates lateral rectus, which abducts the eye.
objective: Identify the muscle affected in CN VI palsy.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: A manic episode consists of persistently elevated or irritable mood and increased energy with decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, grandiosity, and impaired judgment severe enough to cause marked impairment.
vignette: A 30-year-old man has 8 days of euphoric mood, sleeps 2 hours nightly without fatigue, speaks rapidly, spends recklessly, and believes he has special powers. He requires hospitalization.
correct: Bipolar I disorder with a manic episode
distractor_notes: Major depression does not include mania.
Cyclothymia has chronic subthreshold mood symptoms without a full manic episode.
GAD causes excessive worry rather than euphoric grandiosity.
ADHD is chronic from childhood and does not cause discrete severe manic episodes.
key_expl: A full manic episode requiring hospitalization establishes bipolar I disorder.
objective: Recognize mania and bipolar I disorder.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thought/behavior, and negative symptoms with significant functional decline.
vignette: A 23-year-old man has 9 months of auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions, disorganized speech, social withdrawal, and declining function without a mood episode dominating the illness.
distractor_notes: Brief psychotic disorder lasts less than 1 month.
Schizophreniform disorder lasts 1–6 months.
Bipolar disorder requires prominent mood episodes.
Delusional disorder lacks the broad disorganization and hallucination/negative-symptom pattern.
key_expl: Psychotic and negative symptoms with functional decline persisting over 6 months support schizophrenia.
objective: Differentiate schizophrenia from shorter-duration psychotic disorders.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Chronic impaired aqueous humor outflow through the trabecular meshwork raises or dysregulates intraocular pressure and progressively damages the optic nerve, causing peripheral visual-field loss.
vignette: A 70-year-old man has slowly progressive peripheral visual-field loss and optic-disc cupping without ocular pain.
distractor_notes: Lens disease causes cataract, not glaucomatous cupping.
Corneal disease does not produce the characteristic optic-disc changes.
Macular disease causes central, not peripheral, visual loss.
Extraocular muscle disease causes motility deficits.
key_expl: Glaucoma is an optic neuropathy characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell and optic nerve damage.
objective: Identify optic nerve damage in open-angle glaucoma.
